answers.how: Fitting the ball's vertical trajectory gives approximately 2200 px/s², so gravity sets the scale to 0.00445 m/px. The ball's diameter is about 56 px.
The middle billboard is approximately 167 px wide. Using the gravity-derived scale of 0.445 cm/px gives its length.
The left billboard is approximately 174 px high. Multiplying by the gravity-derived scale of 0.445 cm/px gives its height.
The right billboard is approximately 75.5 px high. Multiplying by the gravity-derived scale of 0.445 cm/px gives its height.
The horizontal span between the specified outer edges is approximately 434 px, converted using 0.445 cm/px.

After correcting camera movement using the billboards, the velocity components near 2.50 s are approximately 648 px/s horizontally and 295 px/s vertically. Their magnitude is converted using 0.00445 m/px.
Near 3.00 s, the camera-corrected velocity components are approximately 593 px/s horizontally and 800 px/s vertically. Their magnitude is converted using 0.00445 m/px.
The camera-corrected displacement components from 2.50 to 3.20 s are approximately 428 px horizontally and 331 px vertically. Convert their resultant to meters and divide by 0.70 s.
The camera-corrected displacement components from 2.50 to 3.00 s are approximately 309 px horizontally and 129 px vertically. Their resultant is converted using 0.00445 m/px.
